note: Four non-US members reached HCC patients on an academic mouse HCC model dosed with a rat anti-mouse surrogate and, for penpulimab, a filed MC38 knock-in mouse; camrelizumab monotherapy and two antibody-plus-TKI phase 3s (CARES-310, APOLLO) matched, penpulimab's monkeys missed the immune-related harms the knockout mouse had foretold, and camrelizumab's capillary proliferations were explained only by a post-hoc off-target screen.
label: HCC (anti-PD-1)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The rat anti-mouse PD-1 surrogate is a sibling of the class, not a member; none of the four members binds mouse PD-1 (penpulimab FDA review 2025 states this for penpulimab).
engagement.model: Syngeneic orthotopic mouse HCC (HCA-1 in C3H, RIL-175 in C57BL/6; grafted and genetically engineered) under a rat anti-mouse PD-1 surrogate, with or without apatinib
engagement.note: The HCC mouse models read intratumoral immune changes; no member antibody's pharmacodynamic readout has been compared in HCC patients.
engagement.short: Surrogate-dosed HCC mice; no patient PD test
engagement.quote: In separate experiments, antibody blockade of the programmed death ligand-1 receptor programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) showed antitumor effects in treatment-naive tumors in orthotopic (grafted and genetically engineered) models of HCC.
engagement.judgement: No member antibody has a published HCC-patient pharmacodynamic readout paired with a mouse HCC readout; camrelizumab's phase 1 measured receptor occupancy but no HCC mouse model measured it. Kept as the opener for the disease-model track.

engagement.magnitude_basis: fraction of PD-1 occupied: about 90 % at 0.5 ug/mL in vitro vs 80-100 % on patients' T cells at 1-10 mg/kg (steady-state trough >10 ug/mL)
engagement.population: Advanced solid tumours (AK105-101, Australia; not HCC-specific)
engagement.confidence_note: Review clinical pharmacology section read in passages (pp. 63-64 of the multidisciplinary review). Patients were the Australian phase Ia solid-tumour cohort, not HCC; engagement does not require the context disease. The system is a cell-based in-vitro titration; ex_vivo is the nearest enum.
engagement.model: In-vitro PD-1 receptor-occupancy titration of penpulimab on human PD-1-expressing cells (0.1 ug/mL for 80 %, 0.5 ug/mL for about 90 % occupancy)
engagement.note: FDA set the in-vitro occupancy concentrations beside patient data: PD-1 occupancy on circulating T cells reached 80-100 % from day 2 at every dose from 1 mg/kg.
engagement.short: Patient PD-1 occupancy 80-100% as in vitro
engagement.quote: PD-1 RO reached 80% to 100% starting from two days post-dose for all these cohorts.
engagement.reason: Occupancy readout moved in dosed patients
engagement.judgement: Its own track rather than a monkey track: penpulimab's monkeys carried no occupancy readout, so the only model-side occupancy prediction is the in-vitro titration the FDA used to justify 200 mg. Camrelizumab's phase 1 also measured patient occupancy, but no model-side number was published to pair it with, so it is noted, not scored. The review states both sides in one section, so comparison_stated is true.

dose.magnitude_basis: monkey NOAEL 60 mg/kg every 2 weeks vs APOLLO 200 mg every 3 weeks (about 3 mg/kg): roughly 20-fold dose margin; no exposure multiple stated in the review
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of APOLLO (Lancet Oncol epub 2025-05-08); NCT04344158 has no posted results (checked 2026-11-05). The review gives the monkey NOAEL (pp. 40-47) but I found no stated exposure multiple against the 200 mg regimen, so the margin is a dose ratio. APOLLO's OS was a second interim analysis.
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey 6- and 13-week repeat-dose toxicology of penpulimab (4, 15, 60 mg/kg every 2 weeks; NOAEL 60 mg/kg; no occupancy readout)
dose.note: Monkeys tolerated 60 mg/kg every 2 weeks for 13 weeks with nothing of toxicological significance; APOLLO dosed 200 mg every 3 weeks and met both co-primary endpoints.
dose.short: Monkey margin held; APOLLO met OS and PFS
dose.quote: Median overall survival was significantly prolonged with anlotinib plus penpulimab compared with sorafenib (16·5 months [95% CI 14·7-19·0] vs 13·2 months [9·7-16·9]; HR 0·69 [95% CI 0·55-0·87]; p=0·0014).
dose.judgement: Reached-and-worked rule with decision 16: the monkey stated a tolerated dose (NOAEL 60 mg/kg every 2 weeks, 13 weeks) far above the clinical 200 mg, and APOLLO patients were dosed there without the monkey's (absent) toxicity, so margin_stated true. The pairing is mine: the review and the trial are different documents. Camrelizumab's 3 mg/kg and 200 mg HCC regimens and spartalizumab's 300 mg every 3 weeks came from non-HCC phase 1 occupancy plateaus with no published model-derived target, so they are not scored. The model_id follows the NSCLC tile's monkey track; penpulimab's monkeys read toxicology only.

dose.magnitude_basis: simulated steady-state trough >10 ug/mL in >95 % of patients vs 0.5 ug/mL for 90-100 % in-vitro occupancy: 20-fold
dose.confidence_note: Review clinical pharmacology section read in passages (p. 64); the passage sits in the Applicant-written 'Data' part of the review, with the FDA's dosing conclusion following. The popPK model was fit to 771 patients across tumour types. The efficacy tie to APOLLO (same 200 mg every 3 weeks regimen; PFS HR 0.52, OS HR 0.69) is mine.
dose.model: Population-PK simulation of penpulimab 200 mg every 3 weeks against the in-vitro PD-1 occupancy concentrations (0.1 ug/mL for 80 %, 0.5 ug/mL for 90-100 %)
dose.note: FDA's review states the simulated steady-state trough exceeds 10 ug/mL in more than 95 % of patients, 20-fold above the 90-100 % occupancy concentration; APOLLO used that regimen and met PFS and OS.
dose.short: Simulated trough 20x occupancy target; APOLLO met
dose.quote: with a penpulimab dose of 200 mg Q3W, the steady-state trough concentration in more than 95% of patients was >10 μg/mL, which is 100-fold higher than those at which 80% of the receptors (0.1 µg/mL) could be occupied
dose.judgement: Same by the reached-and-worked rule: the simulated regimen is the one APOLLO used and APOLLO met both co-primary endpoints. Kept apart from the monkey track as in the NSCLC tile: an in-silico model fit to patient PK with no tolerability output, so margin_stated null; the monkey entry carries decision 16. The quote is a verbatim clause of a 58-word sentence.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Earliest in-vivo anti-PD-1 antibody study in a mouse HCC model that PubMed returned; none of the members' sponsors filed a liver model (penpulimab's FDA package used MC38 in PD-1 knock-in mice).
efficacy.model: Syngeneic orthotopic mouse HCC (HCA-1 in C3H, RIL-175 in C57BL/6; grafted and genetically engineered) under a rat anti-mouse PD-1 surrogate, with or without apatinib
efficacy.note: Surrogate anti-PD-1 alone slowed treatment-naive orthotopic HCC; added to sorafenib it worked only with CXCR4 blockade. No member yet in HCC patients.
efficacy.short: Surrogate anti-PD-1 slows orthotopic mouse HCC
efficacy.quote: In separate experiments, antibody blockade of the programmed death ligand-1 receptor programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) showed antitumor effects in treatment-naive tumors in orthotopic (grafted and genetically engineered) models of HCC.
efficacy.judgement: The disease-model track: an academic orthotopic HCC model dosed with a rat anti-mouse surrogate, because no member binds mouse PD-1. Kept apart from the filed MC38 knock-in track (different tumour, host and antibody). No patient-level ex-vivo predictor (organoid or tumour-fragment) has been run with a member in HCC, so there is no patient-level track.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: antitumour effect of surrogate anti-PD-1 in orthotopic HCC mice vs 14.7 % objective response and 74.4 % 6-month survival on camrelizumab monotherapy
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Single-arm for the drug (randomised only between every-2-week and every-3-week schedules); the abstract states no null hypothesis for the co-primary endpoints, so 'met' rests on the authors' reading and on the Chinese conditional approval that followed in March 2020. NCT02989922 results posted 2024-03-15.

patient_trials.quote: the ORR was 34.3% [24/70; 95% confidence interval (CI), 23.3-46.6] in the first-line and 22.5% (27/120; 95% CI, 15.4-31.0) in the second-line cohort per IRC.
The objective response rate was 30.0% (95% confidence interval [CI], 11.9-54.3) in group A and 14.3% (95% CI, 3.0-36.3) in group B.
The observed overall response rate in the capmatinib + spartalizumab arm was 9.4% vs. 10% in the spartalizumab arm.

efficacy.model: Syngeneic orthotopic mouse HCC (HCA-1 in C3H, RIL-175 in C57BL/6; grafted and genetically engineered) under a rat anti-mouse PD-1 surrogate, with or without apatinib
efficacy.note: Camrelizumab monotherapy in 217 pretreated Chinese HCC patients: objective response 14.7 % by central review and 6-month survival 74.4 %, the co-primary endpoints; Chinese conditional approval followed.
efficacy.quote: Objective response was reported in 32 (14·7%; 95% CI 10·3-20·2) of 217 patients.
efficacy.judgement: Same in direction: the surrogate-dosed HCC mice predicted single-agent activity and a member showed durable responses as monotherapy in HCC. Pairing is mine. Magnitude is direction-only because a mouse growth delay and a response rate share no scale. Not neg: the mouse data never fell below a class bar. RESCUE (camrelizumab plus apatinib), the serplulimab phase 2s and the spartalizumab phase Ib/II are listed; the last tested a MET-inhibitor add-on against spartalizumab alone and says nothing about PD-1 blockade.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: 'remarkable reduction of tumor growth' with apatinib plus anti-PD-1 in syngeneic HCC mice vs OS HR 0.62 and PFS HR 0.52 in CARES-310
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of CARES-310 (Lancet epub 2023-07-24) and of the mouse paper (Yang 2021, Cancer Gene Ther, epub 2020-06-12; host strain and antibody clone not named in the abstract). The comparator was sorafenib, not rivoceranib alone, so the antibody's own contribution is not isolated; rivoceranib monotherapy is active in HCC. Final OS (Qin 2025, 10.1016/S1470-2045(25)00543-1) was not read. NCT03764293 results posted 2024-02-06.

patient_trials.quote: Median progression-free survival was significantly extended with anlotinib plus penpulimab versus sorafenib (6·9 months [95% CI 5·8-8·0] vs 2·8 months [2·7-4·1]; hazard ratio [HR] 0·52 [95% CI 0·41-0·66]; p<0·0001).
the objective response rate was 29.3% (95% CI: 18.1-42.7) as assessed by an independent radiological review committee (IRRC) per RECIST v1.1.

efficacy.model: Syngeneic orthotopic mouse HCC (HCA-1 in C3H, RIL-175 in C57BL/6; grafted and genetically engineered) under a rat anti-mouse PD-1 surrogate, with or without apatinib
efficacy.note: CARES-310: camrelizumab plus rivoceranib beat sorafenib on both primary endpoints (PFS HR 0.52, OS HR 0.62), as apatinib plus surrogate anti-PD-1 had in syngeneic HCC mice.
efficacy.quote: Median overall survival was significantly extended with camrelizumab-rivoceranib versus sorafenib (22·1 months [95% CI 19·1-27·2] vs 15·2 months [13·0-18·5]; HR 0·62 [95% CI 0·49-0·80]; one-sided p<0·0001).
efficacy.reason: Mice right for two members in HCC
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens, not a new status: a randomised phase 3 on the same track, now for the combination the mice tested (apatinib plus surrogate anti-PD-1 in a syngeneic HCC model). Same system as the 2015 opener (syngeneic mouse HCC under a surrogate), so not a separate track. APOLLO (anlotinib plus penpulimab vs sorafenib, PFS HR 0.52, OS HR 0.69) is listed as the second member. Serplulimab's phase 3 vs sorafenib (NCT04465734) was withdrawn, so that member has only single-arm phase 2 data. If the atlas requires the anti-PD-1 contribution to be isolated, the 2020 monotherapy entry alone carries the status.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: 74.1 % and 54.5 % tumour growth inhibition at 0.8 and 8 mg/kg in MC38 knock-in mice vs OS HR 0.69 and PFS HR 0.52 in APOLLO
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of APOLLO (Lancet Oncol epub 2025-05-08); NCT04344158 has no posted results. Review pp. 40 and 46-47 read in full; the mouse study (E3174-B1701) is undated, so 2025, the review's posting, is its first public date. OS was a second interim analysis and the comparator sorafenib, so the antibody's contribution is not isolated.
efficacy.model: MC38 colon carcinoma in human PD-1 knock-in (HuGEMM) C57BL/6 mice dosed with penpulimab (Study E3174-B1701, nivolumab comparator)
efficacy.note: Penpulimab's filed model: 74.1 % and 54.5 % tumour growth inhibition at 0.8 and 8 mg/kg; APOLLO then met progression-free and overall survival in unresectable HCC.
efficacy.quote: Median overall survival was significantly prolonged with anlotinib plus penpulimab compared with sorafenib (16·5 months [95% CI 14·7-19·0] vs 13·2 months [9·7-16·9]; HR 0·69 [95% CI 0·55-0·87]; p=0·0014).
efficacy.reason: Mice right for two members in HCC
efficacy.judgement: Separate track from the HCC mice: a filed, product-dosed, non-liver tumour in a knock-in host; what it predicts is class activity, not HCC biology. The model_id matches the NSCLC tile's MC38 track, which pools surrogate and knock-in MC38. Same by direction; a 74 % growth inhibition and a hazard ratio share no scale. The nivolumab comparator in the same study is a non-member and is not scored. Pairing is mine.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The penpulimab FDA review cites PD-1-deficient mice in its nonclinical pharmacology and toxicology sections ('autoimmunity can occur in PD-1-deficient mice'), so model_filed is true.
safety.note: Aged PD-1-deficient mice develop lupus-like arthritis and glomerulonephritis: the class-level prediction of autoimmune harm, untested until a member reached HCC patients.
safety.quote: Aged C57BL/6(B6)-PD-1(-/-) congenic mice spontaneously developed characteristic lupus-like proliferative arthritis and glomerulonephritis with predominant IgG3 deposition, which were markedly accelerated by introduction of a Fas mutation (lpr).
safety.judgement: The class-level autoimmunity model, opened at its first use; same track and slug as the NSCLC anti-PDCD1 tile.

safety.magnitude_basis: off-target VEGFR2 agonism in vitro vs reactive cutaneous capillary endothelial proliferation in 145/217 (66.8 %) HCC patients on camrelizumab monotherapy (Wang 2020)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both papers. The HCC patient rate is from Wang 2020 (J Hematol Oncol, 10.1186/s13045-020-00886-2): RCCEP in 66.8 % of the phase 2 patients, all grade 1-2, and associated with response. The screen is a cell-based in-vitro system; ex_vivo is the nearest enum.
safety.model: Human receptor-proteome screen of camrelizumab (SHR-1210) off-target binding, with VEGFR2 agonism assays
safety.note: Screen run because camrelizumab's capillary haemangiomas were already known; it found low-affinity VEGFR2, FZD5 and ULBP2 binding and VEGFR2 agonism. RCCEP later hit 66.8 % of the HCC phase 2 patients.
safety.quote: As the humanized antibody SHR-1210 causes capillary hemangioma in patients, a unique toxicity amongst anti-PD1 antibodies, we performed human receptor proteome screening to identify nonspecific interactions that might drive angiogenesis.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction, so retro and never same: the haemangiomas were known from camrelizumab's phase 1 before the screen was run. A molecule-specific off-target harm, not an on-target one, so it does not transfer to the other members; no camrelizumab monkey toxicology is public, so the species' silence cannot be scored. Entry dated to the screen (2018); the HCC-specific confirmation came in 2020.

safety.magnitude_basis: lupus-like arthritis and glomerulonephritis in aged knockout mice vs immune-related adverse events (rate and organs not given in the abstract) in pretreated HCC patients
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the abstract gives neither the irAE rate nor the organs, and the regimen included a bevacizumab biosimilar. The camrelizumab monotherapy phase 2 (Qin 2020) reports grade 3-4 treatment-related events in 22 % with AST rise commonest, but its abstract does not label them immune-related. NCT03973112 has no posted results.
safety.note: Serplulimab plus HLX04 in 41 pretreated HCC patients: immune-related adverse events occurred, mostly grade 3 or lower, as PD-1 loss in mice had foretold.
safety.short: Immune-related AEs in HCC as knockout predicted
safety.quote: Most immune-related adverse events were grade ≤3.
safety.judgement: Pairing is mine. Scored same because a member produced immune-related events in HCC patients and the knockout mouse's phenotype is autoimmunity; partial because the organ pattern and severity differ and the abstract carries no rate. Year is the 2022 online date, print 2023.

safety.magnitude_basis: no toxicologically significant findings in monkeys at 60 mg/kg every 2 weeks vs immune-related adverse events in 158/558 (28.3 %) penpulimab-treated patients across all doses, 32.3 % in nasopharyngeal carcinoma at 200 mg every 2 weeks
safety.confidence_note: Review nonclinical pp. 40-47 and the irAE table (Applicant Table 34, p. 177) read; the two sit in different sections, so the pairing is mine. Patient side is the pooled penpulimab monotherapy population (nasopharyngeal carcinoma and other solid tumours; HCC was 6 % of the integrated safety pool); HCC-specific irAE rates for members sit in full texts not read.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey 6- and 13-week repeat-dose toxicology of penpulimab (4, 15, 60 mg/kg every 2 weeks; NOAEL 60 mg/kg; no occupancy readout)
safety.note: Monkeys at up to 60 mg/kg for 13 weeks showed nothing of toxicological significance; 28.3 % of penpulimab-treated patients had an immune-related adverse event, hypothyroidism commonest.
safety.quote: There were no mortalities or penpulimab-related findings of toxicological significance.
safety.reason: Knockout right, monkeys silent, RCCEP retrodicted
safety.judgement: Contra: penpulimab's monkeys, dosed every two weeks for 13 weeks at about 20 times the clinical dose, showed only lymph-node cellularity and erythrophagocytosis, while 28 % of patients had immune-related events; the species can show the lesion (another member's monkeys did on this track in the NSCLC tile), so the silence counts. Imported from nasopharyngeal carcinoma under the transfer rule; a mouse could not have shown it, a monkey could. Spartalizumab and serplulimab have no public monkey toxicology to score, and camrelizumab's is not public either.

safety.model: Mycobacterium tuberculosis aerosol-infected PD-1 knockout (C57BL/6) mice read for survival, lung bacterial burden and inflammatory cytokines against wild-type controls (Lázár-Molnár 2010); filed in penpulimab's BLA and carried into label section 13.2
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Lázár-Molnár 2010 (PMID 20624978); the FDA review's own description of the study (bundle nonclinical section and appendix) read in full. The lone penpulimab TB SAE is read from the review's AK105-304 SAE narrative, not a table.
safety.note: PD-1 loss made Mtb-infected mice die faster with uncontrolled bacterial growth: an infection-exacerbation prediction no member antibody has been compared against in isolation.
safety.short: Mtb-infected PD-1 knockouts die faster; untested
safety.quote: PD-1-deficient mice showed dramatically reduced survival compared with wild-type mice.
safety.reason: Only member TB datum is chemo-confounded
safety.judgement: Opening entry for the infection-exacerbation system the penpulimab review cites (Lázár-Molnár 2010) and the label's section 13.2 carries, so model_filed is true. Kept as its own track rather than folded into the draft's pd1-knockout-mouse (Nishimura 1999): the same genotype, but a different experimental system (aerosol Mtb challenge) making a different prediction (lethal failure to control a primary infection, not autoimmunity), which the run's identity rule separates. No product in the model: germline absence of PD-1, no antibody. Patient side considered: the penpulimab FDA review's AK105-304 combination-therapy SAE list (penpulimab 200 mg Q3W plus gemcitabine and cisplatin/carboplatin, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, n=146) names 'pulmonary tuberculosis' once among SAEs the investigator deemed drug-related, and no TB appears elsewhere in the review. That is the only member-drug patient datum on this prediction: n=1, chemotherapy co-administered (itself a TB risk), a TB-endemic population, no comparator rate and no FDA attribution, so the antibody's contribution is unisolated and, by the checker's standing rule on this tile (efficacy 4 and dose 2 corrected to untested for the same reason), it cannot carry same. PubMed has no peer-reviewed TB case under camrelizumab, penpulimab, serplulimab or spartalizumab; the ICI-TB series and reviews name only non-members.

safety.model: Mycobacterium tuberculosis-infected rhesus macaques infused with a primatized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody (10 mg/kg, six doses from week 2 post-infection) versus isotype control, read by PET-CT, granuloma bacterial load and cytokines (Kauffman 2021); filed in penpulimab's BLA and carried into label section 13.2
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Kauffman 2021 (PMID 33452107) plus the FDA review's full description of the study (10 mg/kg, n=6 per group, dosed weeks 2-13). The Europe PMC full-text fetch returned nothing, so whether the paper itself cites the patient case reports is unverified; the 2020 systematic review of ICI-associated TB (Eur J Cancer, PMID 32375103) predates it regardless.
safety.note: Anti-PD-1 worsened established Mtb infection in macaques; run after patient TB reactivation under non-member anti-PD-1s was known; no member comparison in isolation.
safety.quote: Animals treated with anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody developed worse disease and higher granuloma bacterial loads compared with isotype control-treated monkeys.
safety.reason: Retrodictive macaque model; member datum confounded
safety.judgement: Opening entry for the second infection system the penpulimab review cites and label section 13.2 carries (model_filed true). A separate track from the knockout mouse under the run's identity rule: pharmacological PD-1 blockade of an established infection in a primate, predicting exacerbation of controlled disease, versus germline absence during primary infection in mice predicting failure to survive it. The antibody is a primatized anti-PD-1, not a member (product_in_model false). The study was run after the clinic already knew that anti-PD-1 reactivates TB (16 nivolumab/pembrolizumab cases reviewed in Eur J Cancer 2020), so any comparison later scored on this track is a retrodiction under decision 10 and can only be retro or contra; retrodiction is recorded false here because the status is untested and lint allows the flag only on a scored entry. Patient side considered: the penpulimab FDA review's AK105-304 combination-therapy SAE list (penpulimab 200 mg Q3W plus gemcitabine and cisplatin/carboplatin, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, n=146) names 'pulmonary tuberculosis' once among SAEs the investigator deemed drug-related, and no TB appears elsewhere in the review. That is the only member-drug patient datum on this prediction: n=1, chemotherapy co-administered (itself a TB risk), a TB-endemic population, no comparator rate and no FDA attribution, so the antibody's contribution is unisolated and, by the checker's standing rule on this tile (efficacy 4 and dose 2 corrected to untested for the same reason), it cannot carry same. PubMed has no peer-reviewed TB case under camrelizumab, penpulimab, serplulimab or spartalizumab; the ICI-TB series and reviews name only non-members.
